name: Coronado
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Coronado, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Coronado, CA: Breakfast with Santa, the library's Decorating Day, the Holiday Cabaret, Artisans Alley and Lamb's Festival of Christmas.
lede: Coronado keeps Christmas small town and close to home. Orange Avenue closes for a hometown holiday parade, Santa lights a tree wrapped in more than 18,000 lights, and Rotary elves still deliver presents to island children on Christmas Eve.
celebrates: The season starts on the first Friday in December, when the Coronado Chamber of Commerce runs the Holiday Parade down Orange Avenue and Santa lights the tree in Rotary Plaza near 10th Street, followed by a Coronado Community Band concert. The Hotel del Coronado sets up its beachfront Skating by the Sea rink, and Santa skydives onto Del Beach at its Holiday Festival. Around town, the library hosts a Decorating Day and a Santa storytime, the city serves Breakfast with Santa at the Community Center, school choirs sing at the Artisans Alley craft fair, and families watch the San Diego Bay Parade of Lights from Tidelands Park and the Ferry Landing.
lastyear: The 50th annual Coronado Holiday Parade and Tree Lighting took place on Friday, December 5, 2025. The chamber counted more than 50 parade entries from businesses, clubs and artists, and expected about 17,000 people downtown. The parade stepped off at 6 pm from Orange Avenue and 8th Street toward R.H. Dana Place near the Hotel del Coronado, and at 7 pm Santa lit the Rotary Plaza tree, wrapped in more than 18,000 lights, about two miles of them.
facts: Coronado was incorporated as a city in 1890, and its nickname is the Crown City, a nod to its Spanish name. The Hotel del Coronado opened in 1888, and for 2026 it has themed its holiday season A Holiday Through Time. The Rotary Club of Coronado's Santa Claus present delivery reaches its 97th year in 2026, with Santa and his elves bringing gifts to local children on Christmas Eve.
trains: Coronado has no train station, but getting to the rails is part of the fun. Flagship's Coronado Ferry leaves the Coronado Ferry Landing at 1201 First Street for Broadway Pier and the Convention Center in downtown San Diego, a ride of about 15 minutes for $9 one way for ages 4 and up. From downtown, families can ride the San Diego Trolley or head to Balboa Park for the San Diego Model Railroad Museum, and the Blue Line reaches the 1882 National City Depot museum.

traditions: The Coronado Chamber of Commerce runs a hometown parade down Orange Avenue on the first Friday in December, and Santa lights the Rotary Plaza tree at 7 pm.
Parents drop one wrapped gift per child at a downtown drop off, and Santa and the Rotary elves deliver the presents across town on Christmas Eve, a tradition now in its 97th year.
The Hotel del Coronado builds an ice rink on its beachfront each holiday season, with views of the Pacific.
Children help decorate the Coronado Public Library's children's section and hang handmade ornaments on the library tree.
A craft fair at Village Elementary School where elementary, middle and high school choirs and bands perform to raise money for school music programs.
Families gather at Tidelands Park and the Coronado Ferry Landing to watch the decorated boats of the San Diego Bay Parade of Lights.
kidfact: In Coronado, Santa does not wait for Christmas night. On Christmas Eve he and the Rotary elves deliver presents to Coronado kids in person, a tradition that turns 97 years old this year.
faq: When is the Coronado Holiday Parade?

The Coronado Chamber of Commerce holds the Holiday Parade and Tree Lighting on the first Friday in December. The parade starts at 6 pm at Orange Avenue and 8th Street, Santa lights the tree in Rotary Plaza near 10th and Orange at 7 pm, and the Coronado Community Band plays afterward. The city says all of the activities are free.
How does the Coronado Rotary Santa delivery work?

Parents, grandparents and guardians drop off one wrapped gift per child at the Rotary drop off downtown during set hours in December, labeled with the child's name, phone number and address. Santa and the Rotary elves then deliver the presents to local children on Christmas Eve between 5 and 7 pm.
How big is the Coronado Christmas tree?

The city describes the Rotary Plaza tree as 120 feet tall and adorned with 18,175 lights. The chamber says the lights stretch about two miles, and Discover Coronado and the City of Coronado co-sponsor them. The holiday lights stay on through December at Orange and Isabella Avenues near 10th Street.
Where can kids watch the Bay Parade of Lights in Coronado?

The San Diego Bay Parade of Lights starts at Shelter Island and passes several waterfront communities before reaching the Coronado Ferry Landing. The City of Coronado recommends Tidelands Park and the Ferry Landing as viewing spots and asks visitors to respect private property and parking areas.
Can you take the ferry to Coronado for Christmas events?

Yes. Flagship's Coronado Ferry runs between the Coronado Ferry Landing at 1201 First Street and Broadway Pier and the Convention Center in downtown San Diego. The crossing takes about 15 minutes and costs $9 one way for ages 4 and up.
